question: The graph below shows average carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions per person in the United Kingdom, Sweden, Italy and Portugal between 1967 and 2007. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
question_text_source: User supplied; matched against the reproduced task page
source_type: third_party_reproduction; not a Cambridge publisher-hosted image
verification: Chart opened and visually checked; source-page model answer was not used as numerical truth or a grading label
unit: metric tonnes of CO2 per person

series_summaries.United Kingdom: Highest throughout; starts just under 11, initially nearly level, then declines to just under 9 by 2007.
series_summaries.Sweden: Starts between 8 and 9, peaks just over 10 in 1977, then declines to about 5.5 in 2007.
series_summaries.Italy: Starts just over 4, rises to just under 8 by 1997, then remains level to 2007; overtakes Sweden between 1987 and 1997, around 1990.
series_summaries.Portugal: Starts just over 1, increases to about 5.5 by 2007; growth slows markedly after 1997; lowest or joint-lowest throughout.

approximation_note: Values are visual approximations. Do not present them as exact measurements. Sweden and Portugal converge at the graph's resolution in 2007.
